papers.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.
papers.summary_cn: 本文研究如何将自回归视频扩散模型的端到端单帧响应延迟降至交互式范围。作者分析发现，VAE 解码和 KV 缓存更新等非去噪操作是主要瓶颈，并提出轻量级像素解码器、KV 缓存修复网络以及面向硬件的系统优化。FastFrames 在 480p 下使用两步扩散生成单个潜在帧：1.3B 版本在单张 B200 GPU 上达到 36 毫秒延迟，14B 版本在 8 张 B200 GPU 上达到 45 毫秒，同时保持或提升生成质量。该方法还被应用于相机条件和物理条件视频生成，实现了大幅加速。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 FastFrames，一系列面向低端到端响应延迟的自回归视频扩散模型，并以每帧延迟和每秒响应数衡量交互性。2. 用基于 ConvNeXt 的轻量级因果像素解码器替代 VAE 解码器，将解码延迟从 147 毫秒降至约 1 毫秒，同时保持细节和视觉质量。3. 提出轻量级 KV 缓存修复网络，用于替代对完整 DiT 的额外缓存更新计算，将缓存更新延迟降低约 10 至 20 倍。4. 结合持久化缓存、条件预计算、融合 QKV 投影、注意力序列分段、CUDA Graph 以及跨 GPU 上下文并行等系统级优化，降低 DiT 推理延迟。5. 在 1.3B 和 14B 模型上取得交互式速度：分别达到单 GPU 36 毫秒和 8 GPU 45 毫秒，并将优化迁移到相机条件和物理条件模型。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究自回归、因果和流式视频生成中的实时响应问题，通过 KV 缓存复用与快速更新、轻量级解码、少步扩散和硬件感知优化实现低延迟生成。其相机条件和物理条件实验与动作或控制条件视觉世界模型及闭环交互仿真密切相关：模型能够在连续生成过程中接收新的控制信号并快速产生响应。论文还说明了端到端响应延迟不能仅用 FPS 衡量，而应使用输入到首个受影响 RGB 帧的延迟或 RPS 衡量，这对实时交互系统评估具有直接意义。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的评估主要集中在 480p 文本到视频生成和高端 B200 GPU 上；作者指出未来仍需支持更高分辨率、更轻量的硬件形态，以及在不增加延迟的情况下加入动作条件。相机条件和物理条件模型经过优化后仍比文本到视频模型更慢，部分配置未达到 50 毫秒目标。论文还指出长期一致性和物理合理性仍有待改进。像素解码器需要针对每个具体模型分别微调，不能像通用 VAE 一样在同一模型系列间共享。论文未明确说明在消费级硬件、低资源环境或更长视频上的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 自回归视频扩散模型根据新的观测和输入生成视频帧，因此有望成为交互式视觉体验的媒介。然而，现有模型的速度通常慢几个数量级，无法实现流畅交互。本文提出 FastFrames，一系列在不牺牲质量的情况下实现交互延迟的快速自回归视频扩散模型。我们对当前最先进模型的推理流程进行了分析，发现一些通常被视为固定实现细节的操作（例如 VAE 解码和 KV 缓存更新）实际上占据了端到端推理延迟的一半以上。我们质疑这些组件是否不可或缺，并以轻量级替代方案取代它们。在单张 B200 GPU 上，我们的 1.3B 版本每帧运行时间为 36 毫秒，即每秒 28 次响应（RPS），同时达到了一个速度近慢 8 倍的先进模型的生成质量。我们的 14B 版本在一台配备 8 张 B200 GPU 的节点上每帧运行时间为 45 毫秒，即每秒 22 次响应，并实现了显著更好的视觉质量和真实感。我们展示了 FastFrames 如何支持相机条件和物理条件视频生成等应用中的实时交互。

papers.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
papers.abstract: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.
papers.summary_cn: 论文提出 Invoker-Render，一种由视觉代理驱动的视频渲染框架，将双向离线视频创作与四步因果实时流式生成统一在同一条件接口下。模型可处理语义布局、几何结构等不同代理及粗细不同的控制粒度：粗代理约束场景布局、相机和主体根轨迹，细代理进一步约束关节和表面几何。作者提出 ProForcing 训练流程，依次进行因果教师强制与重采样强制、基于数据历史的四步 DMD/GAN 蒸馏，以及基于自生成历史的长序列训练，以降低流式生成中的漂移。配合 KV 缓存、异构编解码和流水线并行，系统在 1344×768 分辨率下达到 18 FPS。140 个测试序列上的盲评显示其在视觉质量、结构运动、参考保持和总体偏好方面均优于比较方法，并展示了约 30 分钟的稳定赛车生成。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 Invoker-Render，在统一条件接口下结合双向视频创作模型和四步因果流式渲染模型，并支持多种代理表示及多粒度结构控制。2. 提出 Progressive Forcing，将因果适配、少步蒸馏和自生成长序列训练分阶段解耦；其中 RF-DMD 使用数据锚定历史，SF-DMD 再转向连续自生成历史，并结合教师特征相对 GAN 监督。3. 构建约 200 小时的对齐多粒度视频—代理语料库，包含粗细代理、外观参考、结构条件和层次化语言标注。4. 设计面向实时流式渲染的服务栈，包括轻量代理编码器、KV 状态复用、融合执行、跨数据包编解码重叠和异步 CPU 传输，将吞吐提升至 18 FPS。5. 在多种代理、粒度、相机路径和长时赛车场景上验证了结构遵循、外观保持与长时稳定性。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究视频扩散模型的因果、流式和长视频生成，并通过四步蒸馏降低实时推理成本。视觉代理承担显式世界状态和动作/几何控制，使该方法适用于动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环模拟中的“状态引擎—神经渲染器”架构。ProForcing 针对自回归历史中的误差累积和长时 rollout 漂移；KV 缓存、少步生成、编码缓存与流水线并行则对应缓存复用、稀疏/高效推理和实时生成需求。论文还明确指出，当前系统尚未实现与交互式状态引擎的闭环耦合，因此在闭环世界模型方向仍有扩展空间。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，静态前缀 sink 和滑动 KV 窗口会逐步驱逐活动窗口之外的视觉细节，限制了对远期环境信息的记忆；现有方法缺少显式的长期记忆、空间时间检索或持久化 3D 状态缓存。训练时每个 rollout 窗口使用固定代理粒度，尚不支持流式过程中动态切换细节层级。论文还将与交互式状态引擎进行闭环耦合列为未来工作。实验主要基于约 200 小时数据、140 个测试序列和以赛车为代表的长时 rollout，论文未明确说明在更广泛真实交互环境中的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_cn: 视觉代理将显式世界状态模拟与逼真视频合成解耦，为离线片段创作和实时交互式流媒体提供了可控接口。然而，实用的渲染器需要解决两个挑战：上游代理会根据交互需求在粗略布局和精细的关节几何之间变化；流式推理必须在少量因果步骤中运行，同时避免自生成历史不断累积误差。我们提出 Invoker-Render，在统一的结构代理、外观参考和语言条件接口下，将双向创作模型与因果四步流式模型结合起来。该模型在一个对齐的约 200 小时多粒度语料库上训练：在提供精细几何约束时遵循这些约束，在粗略代理下合成合理的局部运动，从而支持运行时选择输入细节。为在双向创作和实时流式生成之间衔接，同时避免步数压缩误差与 rollout 漂移叠加，我们提出渐进式强制训练（Progressive Forcing，ProForcing）。ProForcing 首先训练因果预测器，并利用从训练视频构造的历史将其蒸馏为四步渲染器；随后训练转向连续的自生成 rollout。我们还构建了支持高效流式推理的流水线服务栈。实验表明，该方法能够适应不同代理类型、粒度和相机路径，相比近期流式基线取得稳定提升，并在 30 分钟的赛车 rollout 中保持场景与主体外观稳定。

papers.title: Towards Data-Efficient, Real-Time World Models
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art world models have been used to produce sequences of gameplay that accord with provided user-input actions. However, high quality, consistent gameplay generation often comes at the cost of inference speed, making real-time interactive play and ideation challenging. The substantial quantities of data used to train state-of-the-art models have also made custom training of these models appear impractical, limiting many of their potential uses in creative fields. In this work we demonstrate a major step towards efficient world models: achieving both fast high-quality inference, and improved data efficiency. This is done by replacing the next-token prediction paradigm with a two-stage discrete diffusion-based approach, introducing a lightweight refinement transformer which carries out iterative masked predictions. Building on an autoregressive world model capable of generating highly consistent and complex sequences over minutes (Kanervisto et al., 2025), we achieve substantial model speed-up (79x) with a modest quality trade-off. Additionally, we demonstrate that this model can be trained to reproduce high-quality, consistent gameplay using a dataset containing approximately one day (28 hours) of gameplay data. Our results demonstrate progress towards removing barriers to the use of world models in settings where real-time inference and data efficiency are essential.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 12 figures, 1 table. Includes supplementary material
papers.summary_cn: 本文针对动作条件世界模型的两个关键问题展开研究：高质量长时游戏生成速度慢，以及训练所需数据量过大。作者提出WHAM-RT，将大规模双向骨干Transformer的一次性下一帧预测与轻量级离散扩散细化Transformer结合，并通过可学习寄存器式上下文压缩保留长时序信息。在Bleeding Edge游戏环境中，WHAM-RT在单个H100上最高达到17 FPS，相比WHAM加速最高79倍，并能生成至少5分钟的连贯游戏过程。作者还通过按地图空间覆盖率策划数据，仅用约28小时、单一角色的游戏数据从头训练模型；低数据模型在长时序评估中表现出比完整数据模型更好的稳定性。不过，加速带来了相对于WHAM的质量下降，研究目前也仅验证于单一游戏环境。
papers.contribution_cn:
1. 提出WHAM-RT两阶段世界模型架构：大型骨干Transformer一次性建模时间依赖并生成下一帧草稿，轻量级离散扩散细化Transformer通过迭代掩码预测修正视觉Token。
2. 引入基于可学习寄存器Token的上下文压缩，将长历史压缩为紧凑表示，以降低细化阶段的计算开销。
3. 在Bleeding Edge环境中实现最高17 FPS的实时生成，相比WHAM最高获得79倍加速，同时保持长时域、复杂交互和环境一致性。
4. 设计基于地图空间覆盖和稀有事件采样的数据策划方法，仅用约1天（28小时）游戏数据训练出高质量模型，将数据需求从约1年大幅降低。
5. 通过速度、FVD、JEDI、FVMD、长时域 rollout、消融实验和小规模人类评估，分析了模型的质量—速度权衡及上下文压缩的作用。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点高度相关。本文研究动作条件的交互式视觉世界模型，模型根据连续控制器动作生成游戏视频，并在生成过程中将预测帧和动作更新到滚动上下文中，属于闭环模拟和可控视觉环境建模。其核心方法结合自回归跨帧建模与离散扩散式并行掩码细化，直接针对自回归生成的顺序解码瓶颈。上下文压缩属于面向长视频和长时域生成的记忆/缓存复用机制；一次性帧草稿加少量细化迭代则提升了实时生成能力。论文还讨论了离散扩散、并行解码和效率—质量权衡，但并未提出传统意义上的蒸馏方法或稀疏注意力机制。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，实验仅限于Bleeding Edge单一游戏环境，跨环境训练与适配尚未验证。相较于WHAM，显著加速会降低世界建模质量，尤其可能影响运动一致性并产生抖动；人类评估中WHAM更常被偏好，且WHAM-RT在较高温度下更不稳定。低数据实验仅覆盖单一角色和受限数据分布，因此不能证明对更广泛环境、角色或任务具有同样的数据效率。数据策划模型虽然在长时域指标上更稳定，但总体仍低于WHAM这一质量上限。人类评估规模较小，仅有6名专家、180次判断。论文未明确说明更广泛真实世界场景、不同硬件平台及更长时间尺度下的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 当前最先进的世界模型已被用于生成与用户输入动作相一致的游戏过程序列。然而，高质量且连贯的游戏过程生成通常以推理速度为代价，使实时交互式游玩和创意构思变得困难。用于训练先进模型的大量数据也使这些模型的定制化训练看起来不切实际，限制了其在创意领域中的许多潜在用途。本文展示了迈向高效世界模型的重要一步：同时实现快速、高质量推理和更高的数据效率。具体而言，我们以两阶段离散扩散方法取代下一词预测范式，并引入一个轻量级细化Transformer，执行迭代式掩码预测。在能够生成数分钟内高度连贯、复杂序列的自回归世界模型基础上（Kanervisto等，2025），我们实现了79倍的显著模型加速，同时仅付出适度的质量损失。此外，我们证明该模型仅使用约一天（28小时）的游戏过程数据集进行训练，也能够复现高质量、连贯的游戏过程。结果表明，本文朝着消除世界模型在实时推理和数据效率要求较高场景中的应用障碍迈出了重要一步。

papers.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: World models (WMs) generate driving scenarios beyond recorded logs, enabling the training and evaluation of autonomous driving systems in unseen interactions. However, existing WMs struggle to ensure both behavioral realism and visual fidelity, since they overlook the relationship between vehicle interactions and the ego visual observations. We propose a closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering. First, imitation-learned background-vehicle (BV) policies are fine-tuned with multi-agent reinforcement learning in the closed loop against an end-to-end ego planner that reacts to the rendered images, so that their interaction behaviors match those in real logs. Second, the viewpoints exposed by these interactions guide a per-Gaussian diagnosis of each 3D Gaussian vehicle asset, which attenuates view-dependent colors on under-observed Gaussians and fills never-observed surfaces with generated Gaussians, while preserving the observed appearance. Third, signal lights are rendered according to the driving intentions of the vehicles, by an editor that learns the light states unobserved for a vehicle through counterfactual fine-tuning with a light-state classifier. On long-tail closed-loop scenarios, our method reduces the divergence from real-world interaction behaviors by 85% and improves novel-view vehicle PSNR by 2.0dB over the state-of-the-art WM. The significance of BV light signaling in WMs is shown, as the rendered signal lights conveying BV driving intentions indirectly impact ego driving behaviors in a quarter of the scenarios.
papers.summary_cn: World models (WMs) generate driving scenarios beyond recorded logs, enabling the training and evaluation of autonomous driving systems in unseen interactions.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose a closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model；关键词：world model, interactive, closed-loop, driving
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control
papers.abstract: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding. Purely visual interfaces may lack analytical dynamics, structured states, or explicit collision geometry, requiring internal prediction of action-conditioned process risk. We propose Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) for frozen Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Rather than relying on static state features that cannot distinguish candidate plans sharing an observation, RTS unrolls action-conditioned future latent prefixes in the frozen world model and trains a lightweight risk head with process-violation supervision. To intervene selectively while preserving safe nominal behavior, RTS uses the same predicted prefix-risk criterion as both the search trigger gate and hard feasibility gate: safe nominal plans execute directly, whereas alarms trigger local Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) search to minimize nominal deviation within the feasible set. To prevent isotropic Euclidean minimal modification from shrinking obstacle-directed actions into zero-amplitude stalling, we introduce an amplitude-preserving metric $d_{\mathrm{AP}}$ that retains tangential progression while maintaining a unique zero at the nominal plan. Under unified gating and this unique-zero condition, bypassing safe-state search yields closed-loop trajectories strictly identical to every-step same-kernel search. Evaluated under a process-safety benchmark and Safe Arrival Rate (SAR) metric across five tasks, RTS improves SAR over Direct by 12.67--41.67 percentage points on navigation and articulated control and +2.08/+4.17 pp on Cube/PushT boundary cohorts, maintaining 100% action identity with every-step search while cutting controller time by 17.71%--70.41% across 1,968 paired trajectories.
papers.summary_cn: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) for frozen Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model；关键词：world model, action-conditioned, closed-loop
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: Distilling World Action Models for Efficient Bimanual Manipulation via Anchored Path Matching
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory. We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student. From each state, we continue the teacher to zero noise and use its endpoint and first intermediate state as targets. Modality-routed adapters learn to match both targets from the same starting state. When the two gradients conflict, anchor-priority updates preserve the endpoint gradient and remove the opposing component of the local gradient within each modality. One checkpoint supports 1-, 2-, and 4-step joint generation. The sampling budget can be chosen at deployment without retraining or teacher queries. On RoboTwin 2.0, we train only on Clean demonstrations and evaluate directly on the domain-randomized Random setting. At one step, APM improves closed-loop success over continued base distillation at matched inference budgets by 2.0 percentage points on Clean and 1.4 on Random. Video peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) rises from 30.169 to 32.317 dB, with gains in structural similarity (SSIM) and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). On two real-robot tasks, APM improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times$ relative to the eight-step teacher.Project page: https://jialonglong.github.io/Anchored-Path-Matching/.
papers.summary_cn: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student.

papers.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
papers.abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

papers.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VLA model reason over to support planning beyond pixel-level prediction? We argue that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time. As such, we introduce AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning. Each token is dynamically grounded to a surrounding agent associated with its object's state, such as semantic identity, 3D geometry, motion, and interaction context. AgentWorld learns these tokens through three key processes: explicit geometric grounding, reasoning-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and agent-oriented reinforcement learning. Extensive open-loop and closed-loop experiments under diverse driving scenarios show that AgentWorld enhances planning capabilities, fully exploits visual evidence and agent dynamics, and yields interpretable agent-centric world states.

papers.title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate these properties against references fitted to the video under test, either a scene reconstructed from its own frames or a camera trajectory aligned to the command path with a free scale. Such references can absorb gradual scene deformation and changes in pace and route length, so these errors can pass undetected. We therefore introduce StrideWorld, a benchmark whose references are fixed before the motion they judge. It evaluates scene rigidity against the ground-truth geometry of the start view, and action consistency against the stride of each action, the camera motion of one command. The stride is measured on the model's first steps and then used to test the steps that follow, so each model is judged only against its own steps. Its measurements are validated on rendered videos with known camera motion, and its scores agree with human judgments. Across \nvideos{} videos generated by \nmodels{} open models from $140$ start views, all models but one deform their scenes as the camera moves, with offsets up to $7.3$ times those of a rigid rendering along the same camera path. Most models keep a steady pace when a single action is held. Along composed routes, several models often stall, and most completed routes end away from the positions predicted by each model's own strides. Only the two models that scale commands by the estimated scene depth bring most routes close to these positions. Fine-tuning two models on a few rendered clips removes most of their mid-route stalls. Code, data, and a leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/chuangwang123/strideworld.

papers.title: Plausible Videos Can Lead to Poor Decisions: Diagnosing and CURE-ing World Models for Planning
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as world models for planning, yet a world model that makes plausible, realistic-looking videos that are consistent with the training data can produce poor decisions. We address two key questions: (1) when can we trust a world model for planning, and (2) what should we do when we cannot? We introduce CURE (Certify, Upweight, Rollout, Explore), a certificate-guided technique that assesses whether a world model can be trusted for planning and determines what to do next: whether to upweight the training data to debias the model; roll out more samples at test time; or explore by collecting new data where support (how well the training data cover the planner's decisions) is missing. We deploy CURE across multiple domains, spanning simulated physics based on PhyWorld, MuJoCo arm control, and Language-Table pushing in simulation and on real videos. The decisions our certificate trusts have lower regret than those it does not (e.g., 0.06 vs. 0.38 on Language-Table sim and 0.07 vs. 0.38 on MuJoCo contact), whereas video perceptual quality does not identify good decisions. By focusing on decision quality rather than perceptual quality, CURE lowers regret over the best pessimistic decision rule by 10-25% across support levels, and over world-action models, search and policy learning by 41-64%, given the same data.
